subject.title: Stale client registration replayed to DCR forever; only --reset recovers

question: Should a bare dynamic-client-registration failure invalidate cached client information and retry once, or should automatic recovery require a provider-confirmed stale-client signal?
rationale: The current recovery policy is deliberately limited to structured permanent refresh failures, while the reported DCR error is an unstructured server error that may also represent a transient outage.

options.title: Require a stale-client signal
options.body: Add one retry only when the provider response or changed server identity conclusively shows the cached client registration is invalid.

options.title: Retry all DCR server errors once
options.body: Favor recovery convenience by clearing cached client information after any DCR server error, accepting additional registration churn during transient outages.

options.title: Keep manual reset behavior
options.body: Preserve the current explicit reset requirement until provider-specific DCR error semantics are available.

recommendation.title: Require a stale-client signal
recommendation.body: Add one retry only when the provider response or changed server identity conclusively shows the cached client registration is invalid.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest current-main policy for OAuth credential invalidation was introduced in the merged vault-recovery work.
